listing.name: Star Wars (Atari arcade) / darkuni
listing.summary: Play Atari’s 1983 Star Wars with darkuni’s arcade hardware recreation and your own ROM set.

steps.title: Prepare your own Star Wars arcade ROM set
steps.instruction: Use your own starwars.zip from Atari’s 1983 arcade game, matching the MAME starwars revision 2 set, and keep a separate copy. Put it in your home folder as starwars.zip (%USERPROFILE% on Windows); each Windows, Linux and Mac build finds it there. The game checks the 13 ROM and PROM parts by content. The tagged README lists their sizes, CRCs and accepted original-revision alternatives.

steps.title: Start the Windows or Mac player
steps.instruction: Choose the release tagged V1.1.0b. On Windows, use starwars.exe; it also finds the ZIP beside it. On Intel Mac or Apple Silicon, extract the universal Star Wars.app and open it.

steps.title: Keep your high scores and settings
steps.instruction: Back up nvram.bin and settings.json from the starwars folder under your user configuration directory. This is normally %APPDATA% on Windows, ~/.config or XDG_CONFIG_HOME on Linux and ~/Library/Application Support on Mac.

warnings: The Linux x64 binary requires glibc 2.38 or later, X11 and ALSA libraries.
The publisher does not provide a license for its project code.

presentation.manual_preparation: Before first Play, put your own starwars.zip, matching the MAME starwars revision 2 set, in your home folder as ~/starwars.zip, not into Portcove's install folder, and keep a separate copy. The game checks the 13 ROM and PROM parts by content; without them it shows Star Wars ROMs not found or incomplete, lists the missing parts and suggests putting the ZIP next to the program; keep it in your home folder instead. The package is the publisher's hardware recreation only and contains no ROM data; the publisher does not provide a license for its code. The Linux x86-64 player needs glibc 2.38 or later, X11, ALSA and OpenGL. The macOS player needs macOS 26 or later; upstream signs it ad hoc without notarization and gives no Gatekeeper steps; if macOS blocks the first start, open System Settings › Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. Play has not been tested through Portcove on a Mac. High scores (nvram.bin) and settings (settings.json) are in ~/.config/starwars, or starwars under XDG_CONFIG_HOME, on Linux and in ~/Library/Application Support/starwars on macOS. Those stay outside the managed copy, so Portcove neither backs them up nor removes them, and rollback does not rewind them. Portcove replaces the player; you own the ROM set, high scores and settings.
